name: Kinngait Inuit printmaking and collective distribution
description: Inuit artists and collaborators in Kinngait developed local printmaking and organized distribution through a community cooperative.

impact.note: One community gained printmaking and cooperative sales; a new income and art form there, copied by a few other Arctic communities.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest scoped episode established in these sources; not a global priority claim.

caveats: Inuit graphic traditions long predated this studio. The museum dates the catalogued collection to 1959 and describes its Montreal release in February 1960; release dates should not be collapsed. A Japanese printmaker trained Houston, who later shared methods with Inuit artists; the specific innovations belong to the collective work.

research.note: Independent review checked the participants, dates and the different counts of test-marketed prints and catalogued works against the museum account.
